item.title: D12 · Twelve Paths (balanced edition)
item.description:
D12 · Twelve Paths · Balanced dice method, episode 13
D12: THIRTY COMPLETE SHUFFLES OF TWELVE Each block contains the faces 1 through 12 exactly once in randomized order. Thirty blocks yield 360 five-second slots, thirty minutes of results. Each face appears 30 times, for an ideal probability of 30/360 = 1/12 (about 8.33%) when choosing a slot uniformly. No result repeats within a twelve-slot block, unlike independent rolling.
HOW TO USE THIS AUDIO DIE Seek somewhere inside the numbered-result portion, not the introductory or closing words. Ignore a clipped result and use the next result spoken fully, with each result occupying an equal-length time slot. If playback reaches the coda instead of another complete roll, seek back to the first numbered result. A fair timeline sample means each time slot has the same chance of being selected; ordinary finger-driven scrubbing is not guaranteed to produce uniformly random seek times.
FAIRNESS VERSUS INDEPENDENCE This is a prerecorded deterministic sequence, not a source of fresh live randomness. Exact balanced frequencies guarantee fair outcomes for a uniformly chosen time slot, but a continuous run of results need not have the independence of fresh dice throws. If each playback position is independently sampled uniformly over the result region, those sampled outcomes are independent despite the fixed recording. All experiments use fixed, documented pseudorandom seeds and can be reconstructed.
PRODUCTION Narrated by Brother Rubicon using Kokoro's Lewis voice with the producer-selected Saved 02 treatment. The spoken method explanations are brief; the Brother Rubicon standard introduction is fixed and his observations vary by edition. A distinct whimsical closing coda follows the last valid roll, without a long silence. The coda is not an outcome.
This version has its own Brother Rubicon opening observation and a distinct closing coda; both come from this production edition. The standard introduction is always: I am Brother Rubicon. The die's cast.
Specific opening: In the oldest days, men cast lots to discover what they could not otherwise know. Some of their questions were better left unanswered. I am Brother Rubicon. The die's cast. Twelve faces, thirty shuffled sets. Seek to a random point during the dice rolls. Ignore any number already in progress. Your roll is the next number you hear from its beginning.
A closing remark follows the last valid result, but is not revealed here.

item.title: D100 · Three Complete Shuffles (balanced edition)
item.description:
D100 · Three Complete Shuffles · Balanced dice method, episode 10
METHOD: THREE SHUFFLED COMPLETE SETS OF ONE HUNDRED Shuffle 1–100 independently three times and concatenate those permutations. This gives 300 six-second result slots, exactly 30:00 of outcomes. Every integer 1–100 occurs exactly three times in the full recording, so a uniformly selected time slot produces any particular value with probability 3/300 = 1/100 = 1%. One hundred is a valid result; zero is not.
Within each 100-value set no number repeats. A repeated value may occur at a boundary between sets. That restriction differs from independent live D100 throws, but unlike the previous 300-independent-draw D100 pilot, this balanced edition cannot omit any of its 100 faces.

item.title: 2D6 · Thirty-Six Possibilities (balanced edition)
item.description:
2D6 · Thirty-Six Possibilities · Balanced dice method, episode 9
METHOD: TEN SHUFFLES OF ALL THIRTY-SIX ORDERED 2D6 PAIRS Two distinguishable six-sided dice have 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely ordered pairs: (1,2) and (2,1) are different pairs although they have the same sum. Shuffle all 36 ordered pairs independently for each of ten blocks. That gives 360 results occupying five seconds apiece, or 30:00 of functional audio. The narrator says the first die, the second die, and then the sum.
Each ordered pair appears exactly ten times. The sums 2–12 therefore occur 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10 times respectively. Their probabilities are 1,2,3,4,5,6,5,4,3,2,1 divided by 36. Seven is six times as likely as two or twelve, as it should be. Within a 36-pair block, the same ordered pair cannot repeat, but the same sum can. Consequently, the result sequence is balanced, not sequentially independent.

item.title: D20 · Every Possible Pair (balanced edition)
item.description:
D20 · Every Possible Pair · Balanced dice method, episode 8
METHOD: ORDER-TWO DE BRUIJN / RANDOMIZED EULERIAN CIRCUIT Construct a circular sequence of 400 results from an Eulerian traversal of a directed graph with one edge for each ordered pair of D20 faces (20 × 20 = 400). Every possible ordered consecutive pair, including doubles such as 7→7, appears exactly once as the sequence wraps from its last result back to its first. Each individual face therefore occurs exactly 20 times; its probability on a uniformly sampled time slot is 20/400 = 5%. Four hundred slots at five seconds total 33:20 of dice results.
The pair guarantee is *cyclic*: the final→first pair counts mathematically, but ordinary file playback passes through the closing coda and introduction instead of jumping directly from the last number to the first. To inspect that pair, skip the spoken material on repeat. The construction balances all two-roll patterns, not three-roll patterns, and still isn't a source of fresh independent randomness.

item.title: D20 · One Giant Shuffle (balanced edition)
item.description:
D20 · One Giant Shuffle · Balanced dice method, episode 7
METHOD: ONE GIANT BALANCED SHUFFLE Start with 18 copies of every face 1–20, yielding 360 positions; shuffle the entire 360-entry pool just once. Each face still appears exactly 18 times, and a uniformly chosen time slot has a 5% chance of producing any given face. Unlike the 20-result blocks, identical values can occur consecutively anywhere, so it feels more like ordinary rolls.
Sequential caveat: once outcomes are selected from a finite pool, remaining frequencies change. Adjacent results are not mathematically independent; pairs are not deliberately balanced either. Global equality, not local independence, is what is guaranteed.

item.title: D20 · Shuffled Sets (balanced edition)
item.description:
D20 · Shuffled Sets · Balanced dice method, episode 6
METHOD: EIGHTEEN SHUFFLED SETS The numbers 1–20 are shuffled separately 18 times. Each 20-result block therefore contains every face once, and each face appears exactly 18 times in the full set of 360 five-second time slots (30:00 of results). For uniformly selected time slots, each face has exactly 18/360 = 1/20 = 5% probability.

item.title: Ten Minutes to Disaster
item.description: An original ten-minute suspense soundtrack and functional countdown. It begins with playback, provides a few time warnings, and ends with a decisive bell at exactly ten minutes. These are working pilot releases; details may change with future revisions.

item.title: The Wilderness Oracle
item.description: Eighty original, independent wilderness encounters, each with a subtle boundary cue. Seek and wait for the next complete encounter. Printed numbers and titles are not spoken. These are working pilot releases; details may change with future revisions.

item.title: D100 · Archival Independent Draws
item.description:
ARCHIVAL METHOD: Although the original numbers were generated uniformly, the recorded sequence omits 39, 43, 46, 49, 82 and 85. For seeking, prefer the balanced complete-shuffle D100 edition.
One uniformly generated number from 1 through 100 at a time. Seek to a random point and take the next complete value. The number 100 is read as one hundred. These are working pilot releases; details may change with future revisions.

item.title: 2D6 · Archival Independent Draws
item.description:
ARCHIVAL METHOD: The two dice were generated fairly and independently, but this fixed recording's result frequencies differ from the ideal 2D6 distribution; in particular, the second die shows five 75 times in 300 results. For seeking, prefer the balanced 2D6 edition.
Two independent six-sided dice, followed by their sum. Seek to a random point and use the next complete result. The familiar bell-shaped total distribution emerges naturally. These are working pilot releases; details may change with future revisions.

item.title: D20 · Shuffled Sets
item.description:
Eighteen shuffled groups of twenty, with every D20 face appearing equally often. This is a fully valid seek-to-roll edition; successive rolls inside a group are not independent, which is explained in the method notes.
Thirty minutes of twenty-sided die results. Seek to a random point and use the next complete number. For this pilot, each set of twenty faces is shuffled before the next set. These are working pilot releases; details may change with future revisions.
